audit_findings.title: Ten-year anchor may mix pre- and post-spin businesses
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially includes pre-spin Enhabit owner earnings in the historical OE series and therefore in the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, 2024 and 2023, we incurred legal costs of $ 1.2 million, $ 2.9 million, and $ 15.8 million, respectively, related to ongoing litigation against former executive officers of our home health and hospice business, which was spun off on July 1, 2022.
audit_findings.explanation: The spin is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show which pre-2022 OE components were restated to the continuing IRF perimeter. If positive Enhabit economics remain, the $491.2 million anchor is too high; the amount and materiality cannot be established from the supplied calculations.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2021 OE using continuing-IRF-only statements or disposition-note allocations, then rerun only the trend and anchor selection.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated joint-venture adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, maintenance capex, and working-capital adjustments are applied to earnings attributable to EHC and divided by parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: We retain 50.0 % to 97.5 % ownership in the remaining 67 jointly owned hospitals.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-perimeter mismatch. Its potential scale is material: 2025 consolidated D&A was $327.9 million and net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $192.9 million, versus $566.2 million attributable to EHC. Consolidated add-backs can overstate parent OE, while consolidated capex or working-capital deductions can understate it, so the net direction is not established.
audit_findings.action: Allocate each historical D&A, maintenance-capex, and working-capital adjustment between EHC and noncontrolling interests; rebuild parent-attributable OE and the parent-only cash bridge, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Growth may be valued without its required development spending
audit_findings.magnitude: $680 million-$770 million of implied 2026 non-maintenance capex, computed from $920 million-$995 million total less $225 million-$240 million nondiscretionary capex
audit_findings.mechanism: Base and bull growth increase projected OE while development capital associated with new hospitals and beds is excluded from distributable owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2026, we expect to spend approximately $920 million to $995 million for capital expenditures using cash on hand and borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The implied non-maintenance spending range exceeds both the $491.2 million anchor and the $584.8 million latest OE. Not all of that spending is necessarily required for the modeled 3% or 6% growth, but even a fraction could materially reduce distributable cash flow, making this reasonably capable of changing scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Separate same-store growth from development-driven growth and rerun each scenario after deducting the parent-funded development capital required for that scenario, including ramp-up losses and joint-venture partner contributions.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest can escape the interest-retention rail
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.6 million in 2025; 3.6% of the $491.2 million anchor and approximately $2.43 per share of base value if the full amount were deducted before tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized construction interest avoids current interest expense and may also avoid OE through excluded growth capex and added-back depreciation.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest capitalized was $ 17.6 million, $ 15.2 million, and $ 13.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the amount actually escaped the OE calculation remains unresolved, but the filed 2025 amount provides a conservative scale ceiling. A full $17.6 million deduction would reduce the $68.90 base value by approximately $2.43 per share and would not close the $52.89 gap to the $121.79 market price or alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized interest through capex and depreciation schedules; deduct any escaped recurring amount in the OE series, but no full valuation redesign is required.

audit_findings.title: Puttable joint-venture interests are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $57.9 million at June 30, 2026; approximately $0.57 per share and 0.8% of the $7,009 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A future put exercise could require parent cash in exchange for the noncontrolling partner's ownership and associated future earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain of our joint venture agreements contain provisions that allow our partners to require us to purchase their interests in the joint venture at fair value at certain points in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omits a presently measured redeemable claim, but deducting the entire $57.9 million without credit for acquired JV earnings would reduce value by only about $0.57 per share. That cannot alter the conclusion relative to the $121.79 price. The ultimate direction is mixed because EHC would receive additional JV economics when paying the redemption amount.
audit_findings.action: Obtain put exercise dates, contractual valuation formulas, and parent funding obligations; rerun a paired redemption-payment and acquired-earnings adjustment only if the measured obligation grows materially.

audit_findings.title: Scenarios omit a plausible discrete Medicare rate reset
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $272.1 million of gross annual revenue exposure, computed as 7% of FY2025 Medicare revenue of $3,886.9 million; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A statutory IRF-PPS base-rate cut would reduce revenue and OE before the modeled long-run growth path resumes.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, at its January 2026 meeting, MedPAC approved recommending to Congress, among other things, legislative changes to reduce by 7% the base payment rate under IRF-PPS.
audit_findings.explanation: The 7% figure is a MedPAC recommendation, not a presently enacted cut. The supplied latest filing instead reports a final fiscal-2027 rule expected to increase EHC's Medicare payment rates by approximately 2.3%. The recommendation is nevertheless potentially material because Medicare represented 65.4% of FY2025 revenue, so it should be monitored as a discrete policy risk rather than treated as a current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor congressional and CMS action; if a reduction is enacted or becomes sufficiently probable and measurable, rerun all scenarios with a discrete first-year revenue reset and documented cost, volume, and tax responses.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $25.7 million in FY2024; 5.2% of the $491.2 million anchor and approximately $3.55 per share of base value if fully added to the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially eligible D&A remains expensed instead of being added back to OE.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2024 $25.7m (8.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This treatment cannot overstate value. Even the aggressive assumption that the entire $25.7 million residual is eligible and recurring would raise the base value only from approximately $68.90 to $72.45 per share, still far below the $121.79 market price and insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual using the fixed-asset and intangible-amortization schedules; rerun the anchor only for the portion demonstrated to be an eligible non-economic expense.
